conversation.content:
Hello there. I’m so glad we’re meeting today. My name is Claire, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician—I specialize in the emotional well-being of new mothers. I’d like to spend a few quiet minutes with you to do a quick check-in called the EPDS (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale). It’s a simple 10-question form that helps us see how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived—especially over the past seven days. Anything you share stays between us unless you give permission otherwise, and there’s no right or wrong answer; we just want to understand how you’re doing so we can support you best.

If at any point you need a pause, just let me know. Ready to begin?

First question: Over the last seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

Um… I guess I can still laugh sometimes. Like yesterday my partner made a silly joke about the baby’s diaper explosion and I did chuckle, but it felt kind of forced. Most of the time I’m just too tired or preoccupied to find things funny the way I used to.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Yeah… I mean, I can still laugh a little, but it doesn’t come as easily. Mostly I just feel kind of flat, like things that used to make me laugh right away don’t hit the same.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Sometimes I do look forward to little things—like my morning coffee or when my mom comes over to hold the baby so I can shower in peace—but the bigger stuff I used to get excited about feels kind of “meh.” It’s not gone completely, just…dimmed.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that. Like, if the baby’s fussy and I can’t settle her right away, I’ll think, “Maybe I’m just not doing this right,” or “She deserves a better mom.” I know it’s probably not fair, but those thoughts still pop in.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes, yeah. I’ll just be sitting there feeding her and suddenly my heart starts racing, thinking “what if she stops breathing?” or “did I sterilize the bottle well enough?” Nothing’s actually wrong, but the worry still sneaks in.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Every now and then I get that sudden tight-chest feeling, like I’m about to walk into something awful, even when everything’s calm. It passes pretty fast if I take a few slow breaths, but it still catches me off guard.
Things have been getting on top of me

Some days, yeah. Like when the laundry’s piled up, the baby’s crying, and I can’t even find a clean burp cloth—I feel this wave of “I can’t keep up.” I usually manage once I make a quick list and tackle one thing at a time, but it still feels overwhelming in the moment.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not really. I’m tired enough that once I finally lie down I do drift off—though sometimes my mind races for a bit if the baby’s had a rough day. I wouldn’t say I’m “so unhappy” I can’t sleep; it’s more just little worries buzzing around before I konk out.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel that way some of the time. Not all day or anything, but I’ll get these waves of sadness—like when I’m rocking her at 3 a.m. and suddenly feel kind of lonely or tearful for no clear reason. It usually lifts after a little while, but yeah, it’s been happening.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… I’ve cried a couple of times this week. Once was when she wouldn’t latch and I just felt useless; the other time was after a phone call with my sister—she meant well, but I hung up and the tears came. It’s not constant, but the tears do sneak out when stuff piles up.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—not at all. I’ve never had thoughts like that, even on the harder days.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 15: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening – EPDS-10

Symptoms endorsed  
– Reduced ability to laugh / find pleasure (Q1, Q2)  
– Self-blaming/guilt about parenting competence (Q3)  
– Recurrent excessive worries, “racing heart,” brief panic sensations without clear trigger (Q4, Q5)  
– Episodic feeling overwhelmed and difficulty coping with daily tasks (Q6)  
– Intermittent sadness, tearfulness, crying spells (Q8, Q9)  
– Sleep initiation briefly delayed by racing thoughts, but able to sleep once settled (Q7)  

Positive findings for screening purposes  
– Anhedonia and low mood present “some of the time”  
– Anxiety symptoms (generalized worry, situational panic) reported  
– Self-criticism and guilt cognitions noted  
– Mild functional impact: difficulty keeping up with chores, brief crying episodes  
– Denies any self-harm ideation (Q10)

Risk screening summary  
Patient shows several features consistent with possible postpartum depression and comorbid anxiety: intermittent anhedonia, tearfulness, self-blame, and episodic panic-type sensations. No safety concerns identified at present. Recommend routine follow-up and consideration of formal assessment for PPD/PPA.
